section.title: Late-Night Conversations
section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: Above all a eulogy: every speaker laments his loss, tells how they bonded with him and what they loved about him, and celebrates him. The brief asks for nine people on their feet in one room, each saying what there is to say about the dead man: a eulogy, not a two-voice dialogue. Spine is mixed: Thomas is an original character and not in the corpus, so no event or scene names him; sections anchor on the occasions his notes place him in (the Pragia aftermath, the run-up to Omega-4, Tuchanka, Rannoch, the Citadel shore leave, Grissom, the final push) and the speaker's own record of those. Jack holds the first and last turns (~2,500 words each, long as asked), the other seven run 450-1,000 (Grunt, EDI, James short and blunt; Liara, Joker, Tali fullest). Nine sections is inside the form's 6-14 range. Each turn opens by picking up the one before: Jack's grief to Tali's engine room, Tali's hospital-and-hands to Joker's bad days, Joker's jokes to Liara's late nights, Liara's mother story to Grunt's blunt question, Grunt's kitchen guarding to James's training and banter, James's Hammer glimpse to Wrex, Wrex's speech to EDI's data, EDI's four-leaf-clover tally back to Jack. Alcohol and music run through the turns as the room's furniture (Thomas's disco, pop, rock, rap, metal, folk, gabber, electro, and black-metal playlists, ryncol, the taped-up recipes), not as a section of their own. Canon branch: genophage cured, Wrex leads the krogan, geth-quarian peace (Legion dead), Grunt alive, Thane dead; crew do not know what Shepard chose, and his death is unconfirmed. Thomas's unfinished poems for Jack are private to Jack; the French lines are his to be quoted sparingly and, per memory rules, never verbatim-perfect by anyone but Jack.

promises: Liara answers Joker's jokes with deadpan precision, then admits Thomas is the one she told things she tells no network

Late-night talks on the SR-1 and again on the SR-2: the opposite temperament, soft and intellectual. He did not just listen; he talked, a lot, and argued. His theory, delivered with a philosopher cited badly (garbled Kropotkin or Bookchin, names and quotes wrong): the Prothean empire's authoritarian control, one species ruling all the others, was probably what doomed it; and his teasing that maybe that empire appealed to her because asari matriarchs earn power by age, a kind of gerontocracy. She argued back; she now thinks he was half right and she never told him
He told her about his mother, and what she did with that knowledge (she kept it, filed nowhere), she talked about hers. The similarities
Coffees on the Citadel and what she learned of his Rouen; the Normandy, the name of the ship, and a joke he stopped telling
She is told, in the grief, that Thessia and the Protheans' last stand were the one subject he never made lighter, and that he wrote her something she has not yet read
This is a eulogy: lament the loss, tell how you bonded with him and what you loved about him, and celebrate him; sad in your own way, never a lore recital

required_facts.fact: After killing the yahg Shadow Broker on Hagalaz in 2185 and taking over his information network, Liara T'Soni ran the organization from the Broker's aging storm-riding ship, with the drell Feron and the renamed Info Drone "Glyph" assisting her. Only a handful of people, such as Admiral Hackett, knew the leadership had changed; on the black market, agents merely sensed the Shadow Broker had "gone soft." Sometime shortly before or during the opening of the 2186 Reaper invasion, Liara learned that the Illusive Man had tracked her down and intended to seize the Shadow Broker Base for Cerberus. Knowing the old ship could not survive spaceflight and expecting an assault, Liara and Feron loaded as much of the base's information drives and communications equipment as they could aboard a shuttle and escaped as Cerberus ships closed in. Liara then remotely piloted the abandoned base into a Cerberus cruiser, destroying both vessels. Liara relocated her operation to the renovated Normandy SR-2, setting up the Broker equipment in Miranda Lawson's former quarters and resuming her eavesdropping and resource-brokering in support of the war effort. Her network of agents remained largely intact, though the war steadily thinned their numbers, and some of the Broker's caches were left scattered across the galaxy awaiting recovery. Assorted technology salvaged from the wreck of the base was later contributed to the construction of the Crucible. Liara made no move to reveal her identity, and long-time underlings such as Barla Von never learned of the change; a surviving Urdnot Wrex might only make sly allusions to it.
The Shadow Broker Base on Hagalaz is deliberately crashed into a Cerberus cruiser, destroying both ships
Cerberus fails to capture the Shadow Broker network
Liara and Feron escape with the essential data drives and communications gear
Liara reestablishes Shadow Broker operations aboard the Normandy SR-2 for the duration of the Reaper War
Salvage from the wrecked base is later used to help build the Crucible
Some of the Broker's resources remain scattered across the galaxy for later recovery

Acquired automatically after Priority: The Citadel III, this mission takes Commander Shepard to the asari homeworld Thessia. With the Reapers devastating asari space, Asari High Command finally discloses a long-hidden Prothean artifact housed in a temple to the goddess Athame that may reveal the location of the Catalyst. Shepard, Liara T'Soni, and a third squadmate (Javik's commentary is notable if he is brought) land in an active war zone where asari commandos under an officer named Kurin are barely holding a defensive line. The team fights through heavy Reaper forces - Banshees, Brutes, Ravagers, Marauders, Harvesters and Husks - and passes close by a capital-scale Reaper walking through the ruins. Kurin eventually pulls her surviving soldiers out against orders. Reaching the temple, Shepard finds the science team dead. Liara triggers a concealed Prothean beacon containing a VI called Vendetta, a construct left from the previous cycle. Vendetta reveals that the asari secretly built their technological, cultural and military lead on studying this forbidden Prothean cache in violation of Council law, and confirms that the Catalyst needed to complete the Crucible is the Citadel itself. Before the VI can finish, Kai Leng arrives, having tracked the team, and fights Shepard. Though beaten back, Leng uses a Reaper's arrival as a distraction to knock Shepard down, seize Vendetta and the Catalyst data for the Illusive Man, and escape aboard his gunship, which levels the Temple of Athame as it departs. Back on the Normandy, a defeated Shepard reports the loss to the asari Councilor, and the squad gathers in the War Room to work out where Cerberus has taken the data. Thessia falls to the Reapers.
Thessia falls to the Reapers with catastrophic asari casualties
The asari admit their advantage was built on a hidden, illegal Prothean archive

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. scenes.title: The Party at Shepard's Apartment
scenes.when: 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the clone was stopped and the Normandy retaken, before Cronos Station
scenes.where: Shepard's personal apartment on the Wards — two floors, kitchen, bar by the window, poker den, balcony, hot tub, rock garden

beats.text: Joker suggests the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy. Shepard buys Party Provisions from the kiosk at the bar on the second floor of the Silver Coast Casino for 100 credits, then sends the invitations from the private terminal in the apartment office.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez and Samantha Traynor are automatic. Everyone else is an optional invite, and only surviving squadmates whose Mass Effect 3 arcs are finished can come at all.

Absences nobody explains: Gardner, Allers, Chakwas, Chambers, Adams, Donnelly and Daniels are all missing. Traynor mentions in the kitchen that Chakwas is dealing with a medical emergency on the Citadel. The rest are simply not addressed.
Glyph asks the Commander what kind of party this is — quiet or energetic — and the answer sets the opening conversations. The groupings themselves are set by the guest list, not the theme.

Opening arrangement: Liara and Traynor in the kitchen with Tali, Samara and Garrus. EDI and Joker at the bar by the window with Miranda and Jacob. James and Cortez on the couches by the piano with the Virmire survivor and Jack. Wrex and Grunt upstairs on the balcony with Zaeed and Javik. Kasumi flits between the bar and the kitchen, uncloaking to interject.

Wrex and Grunt spend the opening trading krogan insults over who is stronger — Grunt calling Wrex a fossil and belittling his age. If the mood is energetic they headbutt each other to settle it and Shepard has to stop them before the furniture goes.
Grunt tells Wrex that two of Aralakh Company's recruits had opposed his appointment, and that only one of them had to be dealt with, the other having been killed in a fight.

Garrus's verdict on the place is that it would be a good place to retire, its sightlines appealing to his sniper sensibilities. He complains at a quiet party about the lack of hard drinks and at an energetic one dares Shepard to try the swill on offer.

Traynor cannot get over the size of the apartment — the electric bill alone would have covered her college tuition. Tali's version is that the same bill would have bought her an air conditioner for her suit, which she does not have, and it gets hot in there.
The group toasts the Normandy. Traynor admits she still feels like an outsider next to people who have histories with Shepard, and everyone weighs in.

Traynor gets everyone recounting how they met Shepard. Tali's memory is that all she could think about was hoping Shepard had showered, because her filter needed replacing and humans carry a lot of germs. Liara notes that three years on she is drinking Shepard's booze through a straw, and calls that progress.

Second phase, energetic: Liara and James argue on the balcony about whether biotics or muscle wins, with Jacob, Miranda, Jack, Kaidan and the Virmire survivor taking sides. James shows off his "fine example of peak physical form"; Liara says she is going to challenge him to a pull-up contest, which gives him pause. When James jabs at "flawed implants," Kaidan shoots back with how hard he has worked and his resulting ability to Reave, drawing trepidation from Liara and Jacob. Shepard picks a side. If Shepard backs biotics, Liara lifts him off the floor with no visible effort and Kasumi uncloaks to goad him into sit-ups; if Shepard backs muscle, the push-ups happen instead and Kaidan is flabbergasted, though Shepard can comfort him by saying that his kind of physical excellence is Shepard's kind too.

Second phase, energetic, at the bar: Joker gets ganged up on by Cortez, Garrus, Wrex and Javik or Zaeed over refusing to keep a sidearm in the cockpit. Garrus's line is that a weapon he cannot get to is no weapon at all. Wrex offers Tuchanka as the harshest planet alive and dares anyone present to last a day there, says krogan parties involve a lot of violent deaths, and announces he needs to shoot something. If Shepard keeps the mood up and backs the shooting practice, he makes good on it — bottles on the counter, with Javik and Zaeed joining in.

Second phase, energetic, at the door: Grunt works the vid-phone as bouncer, distinguishing fake salarian lip-hair from the real thing and establishing that Shepard has no half-brother named Sheppy the Volus. He is briefly tempted by cookies and turns them away anyway.

Second phase, quiet: Grunt dares Wrex into a drinking contest and will not accept his excuses, goading him with "logic is for salarians" and the observation that the great Urdnot Wrex has backed down from a challenge. Elsewhere Liara and James compare the SSV Normandy with the SR-2 in the den, with Tali acting out both ships' handling and engine noise and reporting that the SR-2 is harder to perform. Garrus and Zaeed stand on the balcony discussing how to make the apartment defensible. Kaidan, Joker and Samantha discuss EDI on the second floor.
Traynor and Joker — or Traynor and EDI, extremely awkwardly — work through Traynor's recorded opinion of EDI's voice, while Tali nearly poisons herself with cheese trying to change the subject.

Third phase, quiet: Tali ends up on the floor of the downstairs bathroom, wasted and barely comprehensible, having got an omni-tattoo at Jack's suggestion. Shepard tells her to get some rest and hears fragments of her muttering while passing the door afterwards. Grunt is wherever the food or the drink is, announcing his hunger. Liara and James play cards in the den with Javik and a cloaked Kasumi, Glyph dealing if Shepard sends it there.

Third phase, energetic: Grunt is wasted under the running shower upstairs, muttering about being a Space Cowboy, asking whether someone is a wizard, mourning that hanar cannot wear sweaters and reporting that he found a blue rock for Liara. Downstairs the dancing starts between the kitchen and the conference room — Traynor, Cortez, Jack, Samara, Garrus and Tali — with Glyph setting up the floor if sent. Kasumi is in the downstairs bedroom closet going through Shepard's underwear drawer.

Garrus on watching Shepard dance: record it and broadcast it at the Reapers, because they will either run, melt down, or fall in love. Someone starts reciting the periodic table; at "element 69" the humans snicker and Garrus reminds them it is thulium.

Garrus's quiet-party alternative is micro-filaments — tiny explosives laid in a grid across the glass by the door that shred anyone coming through — coordinated with Zaeed over comms, and he later gets to name a booby-trapped coffee maker "caffeine rush".

At the end Shepard assembles everyone by the couch for a group photo. Couples face each other; everyone else looks at the camera. The photograph hangs afterwards by the downstairs bar, opposite the fireplace.

variants.text: Miranda and Jack end up in the den insulting each other. Shepard can push them to reconcile or egg them on; Kasumi uncloaks either way and makes it worse.
Liara calls the apartment the "Shepard-Vakarian love nest"; if Shepard is with someone else, Garrus is the one making the love-nest joke and promising not to interrupt.

Ashley sits with James by the ground-floor couches in the first phase, teasing Cortez. In an energetic second phase, if she and James are both unromanced, James tries to recruit her to his side of the biotics-versus-muscle argument; she flirts back and takes an interest in his physique, and if Shepard encourages the two of them the night pushes them closer without anything coming of it — James tries out a line of Spanish on her that only leaves her asking him to repeat himself. If either of them had been turned down by Shepard first, Ashley alternates between attraction and rejection instead and declines to back James in the argument. During a relaxed third phase, if Wrex is present he recounts being ready to kill for the genophage cure back on Virmire and asks Ashley whether she would have shot him; she says without hesitation that she would have if he'd left her no choice, and Wrex says he respects her for it.

beats.text: Between missions Shepard draws Liara T'Soni out about her parentage. She explains the asari term "pureblood" — the child of two asari, spoken of by some as wasteful because "nothing has been gained," and cruel to say to a pureblood's face.

Liara believes she is one. Matriarch Benezia never named her other parent; Liara has concluded her "second parent" was another asari, which she offers as the reason for Benezia's silence and the humiliation Benezia wished to avoid. She finds the subject painful, and admits she has long wondered who her "father" was and what passed between her parents.

*Main article: Lair of the Shadow Broker (mission)* Shepard is sent information on the Shadow Broker obtained by Cerberus. Shepard travels back to Illium and passes this information onto Liara, who examines it and determines that Feron is indeed alive, and in the custody of the Shadow Broker. After surviving an assassination attempt by a rogue Spectre working for the Shadow Broker, Tela Vasir, Liara, with assistance from Shepard and the information obtained from Cerberus, travels to the Shadow Broker Base on the planet Hagalaz. There, they find Feron being tortured for his previous betrayal of the Broker. Unable to remove the drell from the device holding him down without killing him, Liara and Shepard confront the Shadow Broker, killing him in the process. Now free from the Shadow Broker's custody, Feron opts to remain in the Shadow Broker's base so he can assist Liara, who has taken over as Shadow Broker following the previous Broker's death. He remains unsure what he will do afterward. Liara expresses great concern for Feron, worried his ordeal has left him mentally scarred. In conversation with Shepard, he mentions using his drell ability to slip into old memories to escape the torture. Shepard can ask Liara if she is romantically involved with Feron, and her answers will differ slightly depending on whether or not Shepard is in a relationship with Liara, but both result in Liara denying it. However, her response is somewhat ambiguous if Shepard is not romancing Liara. She points out that at this time, Feron is too emotionally unstable for a relationship and that it would be irresponsible "to take advantage" of the situation. Asking Feron about his relationship with Liara will result in him saying that Liara is a far better friend than he deserves. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

In 2185, the Shadow Broker is being pursued by Liara T'Soni due to Feron's capture. Unbeknownst to Liara, the Broker has a double agent in her employ named Nyxeris to monitor her progress and, when possible, to kill her. It is also heavily implied by Liara that the Shadow Broker is an individual. Thane Krios also mentions that some years ago, batarian mercenaries employed the Shadow Broker to learn Thane's identity, and later used this information to murder his wife, Irikah.

**Prerequisite:** Lair of the Shadow Broker and Horizon (mission) A message from Cerberus is sent to Shepard's private terminal after completing the mission on Horizon: **Shadow Broker Intel** --- To: Shepard From: Cerberus Information Processing We're aware that your old friend Liara T'Soni has been hunting for the Shadow Broker for several years. We wouldn't mind helping her in that hunt, given the Broker's past work for the Collectors. We recently uncovered some information that might give Liara a lead on where to find the Shadow Broker's base of operations, but unfortunately, she doesn't have much faith in Cerberus intel. If you'd visit Illium and pass it on to her as a gesture of goodwill, we'd appreciate it. On the Galaxy Map this mission is titled *Give Liara Intel*.

Lair of the Shadow Broker was a Mass Effect 2 mission in which Commander Shepard helped Liara T'Soni track down the Shadow Broker. It became available after the DLC install and the Horizon mission, triggered by a Cerberus message on the Galaxy Map titled "Give Liara Intel," offering intel on the Broker's base because of his past work for the Collectors. The mission ran without a break from Illium to its end and featured mostly shielded enemies.

On Illium, Shepard delivered the intel to Liara in her office; the data also revealed that Feron, Liara's drell partner who sacrificed himself two years earlier, was still alive. Arriving at Liara's apartment, Shepard met the asari Spectre Tela Vasir investigating an assassination attempt on Liara. Clues led to Sekat, an information broker at the Dracon Trade Center, which exploded as the squad arrived. Fighting through the Shadow Broker's private army with Vasir, Shepard found Liara alive; Liara exposed Vasir as a long-time Shadow Broker asset who had killed Sekat and taken his data. Vasir fled, leading to a firefight, a skycar chase through Nos Astra, and a rooftop battle at the Azure hotel that ended with Shepard killing Vasir, who justified her betrayal as the price of intel that saved lives and accused Shepard of hypocrisy for working with Cerberus.

The trail led to the Broker's ship orbiting in the perpetual storm band of Hagalaz. Shepard, with Liara as a mandatory squadmate, fought across the ship's exterior amid lightning capacitors and maintenance drones, defended a door during a long five-wave siege, and pushed inside to free Feron. Confronting the Shadow Broker revealed him to be a yahg, taken from his homeworld and having killed and replaced the original Broker decades earlier. After a three-stage boss fight, Liara dropped an electrified fluid tank to overload his barrier and kill him. Liara assumed the Broker's identity and network, becoming the new Shadow Broker, and granted Shepard permanent access to the base. If Shepard had romanced Liara in Mass Effect, she later returned Shepard's dog tags recovered from the Normandy wreck. Rewards included 90,000 credits, element zero and palladium, and Heavy Pistol Damage and Damage Protection upgrades. Cut content included early plans to rescue Liara from the Broker or to make Shepard the Shadow Broker.

Feron was a drell information trafficker who described himself as "an information trader. Not a slaver." In Mass Effect: Redemption, set after the destruction of the Normandy SR-1, Liara T'Soni hired him to help find Commander Shepard; he reported that Shepard was neither dead nor alive. Ambushed by Blue Suns sent by the Shadow Broker to delay Liara, the pair were saved by an unknown sniper, then encountered Cerberus agents, including Miranda Lawson, and were brought to the Illusive Man, who revealed the Shadow Broker was working with the Collectors. Feron admitted he had been ordered to lead Liara away from Shepard but chose to help her instead.

Feron took Liara to Afterlife on Omega, where Aria T'Loak resided, and learned where the Blue Suns would bring Shepard's body. He spotted the Broker's enforcer Tazzik but missed his ship with a turret, letting Tazzik flee Omega with the body. Feron revealed he had never stopped working for the Shadow Broker, which they could exploit to track Tazzik. The two infiltrated the Broker's base on Alingon, with Feron passing Liara off as his prisoner; he downloaded the Broker's dealings while Liara distracted a hologram of the Broker. Feron confessed Cerberus had recruited him and that he and the Illusive Man had planned for Feron to snatch the body. When a Collector exposed him as a traitor, Feron held off Tazzik so Liara could escape, and was captured.

In Mass Effect 2, Liara mentioned a "friend" lost during her search. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, Liara, Shepard, and Cerberus intel led to the Shadow Broker Base on Hagalaz, where Feron was found being tortured on a device that could not be removed without killing him. Liara and Shepard killed the Shadow Broker; Liara took over the role, and Feron chose to stay and assist her, mentally scarred and using his drell memory recall to survive the torture. In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard helped Liara take the Broker ship, Feron helped evacuate it during a Cerberus attack, became one of Liara's agents controlling Terminus operations (to Tazzik's dismay), and emailed Shepard offering information via Glyph. If Shepard did not help overthrow the Broker, Liara hired mercenaries to storm the lair and Feron did not survive.

“I know your every secret, while you fumble in the dark.” *Main article: Lair of the Shadow Broker (mission)* If Commander Shepard obtains certain information from Cerberus, the opportunity to team up with Liara T'Soni to confront the Shadow Broker appears. #### Identity After tracking down and infiltrating the Shadow Broker's ship, Shepard and Liara break into the Broker's intel center and confront him in person. The Shadow Broker is revealed to be a member of a pre\-spaceflight race called the yahg. Liara surmises that because the yahg were not discovered until 2125 CE and the Broker's ship is considerably older than that, this yahg usurped the original Shadow Broker years ago and has been running the organization ever since. In the Dossiers terminal found in the ship's intel center, a personal file about the Shadow Broker can be read. The file's messages reveal that after the yahg's homeworld Parnack was discovered and then declared off\-limits in 2125 CE, the original Shadow Broker had his operatives abduct a yahg for him to study. The captured yahg proved highly intelligent and adaptable. With the Shadow Broker's support, the yahg killed the operative that was monitoring him and assumed the operative's identity, attaining a high rank within the organization as "Operative Kechlu". Sometime later, the Shadow Broker became aware that "Operative Kechlu" was a threat and attempted to eliminate him, but was beaten to the chase by "Kechlu". The yahg seamlessly took on the role of Shadow Broker and maintained the organization for the next six decades. #### Future Plans At some point during his reign, the Shadow Broker became aware of the Reapers and the true nature of the Collectors. Liara T'Soni suggests his dealings with the Collectors were a selfish and ill\-conceived attempt to ensure his own survival from the Reapers' coming genocide. Ultimately, the Shadow Broker was never given the chance to further his plans. #### Fate Liara, Shepard, and a third teammate attempt to battle the Shadow Broker in his own office. The Broker manages to incapacitate the third squadmate before the fight even begins. It takes Shepard and Liara extensive teamwork to catch the yahg off guard, turning his own kinetic technology against him as he dies in a fiery explosion. With the death of the yahg Broker, Liara T'Soni steps into the role of Shadow Broker herself. As Shepard and Liara had killed the few operatives aware of the Broker's true identity, Liara could take over without anyone else in the organization suspecting a transition. Liara is well aware of the power at her disposal, capable of starting a war in ten minutes if she wanted to, but vows to not abuse her position and to help Shepard find a way to combat the Reapers. |  | ***“You've got to walk your own path...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Homeworlds** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.page: Storming the Broker's Ship and Freeing Feron
evidence.text: Storming the Broker's Ship and Freeing Feron. 2185, during Lair of the Shadow Broker, after the death of Tela Vasir on Illium the Shadow Broker's storm-riding ship in the atmosphere of Hagalaz, Sowilo system, Hourglass Nebula With comms glitching, the Broker's agents called in for orders. Liara answered in the Broker's modulated voice, told them it was a hardware fault, and ordered every operation to report within one solar day. Feron came in with a drawn pistol, then lowered it. Liara said she was now the Shadow Broker. Shepard could hold her as she wept that her two-year hunt was finally over; she granted Shepard permanent access to the base and its network.

|  | ***“I said get back!”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Redemption** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | - The planet's natural electromagnetic shroud made Alingon a perfect location for a command center for the Shadow Broker, only he has the technology that can reliably cut through the interference, but it forces his hirelings to come to the planet in person for orders and to make any calls on his behalf offworld; essentially working as additional security for his information network. Liara T'Soni and Feron followed Tazzik to Alingon in an effort to retrieve Commander Shepard's body.
